title: Leaf-script request
description: One batch of leaf scripts to run on the Zipp engine without a workflow graph: `oaiy script` reads it, `oaiy script --serve` reads one per `batch` line, and the Desktop's script host sends it. Every job runs on its own fresh Engine, in order; the reply is `script-result.schema.json` with one entry per job in the same order. A request with ANY malformed job is refused WHOLE (`{v, error}`), nothing runs. The requester supplies every file, entry point, hook name and wrapping; OAIY names none. Data (`globals`, `args`, `source`, `files`) crosses into the guest only as JSON literals, never as program text. A Python job may name `modes` of the request's `profile` instead of carrying a file set: the runner then builds the project from the profile and reports the author's own line numbers, still with nothing of its own in it.

identifier.description: Owned by the profile schema, so a profile validates on its own.

budgetMs.description: Wall-clock hint for a host watchdog. The runner itself does not enforce it; a host that does reports `timeout`.

instructionSteps.description: Instruction budget for this job, overriding the profile's. Unset: the engine default.

files.description: Module name (or `name.py`) to source. Modules import one another by name; nothing else can be imported.

mode.description: `program`: indirect eval, completion value. `body`: `new Function(source)()`. `auto`: decided by parsing, a script or else a function body. `entry`: `source` declares `entry`, called with `args`. `parse`: ONE expression, never invoked — parsed by the runner (`oaiy script` uses acorn, so `1); x = (1` is `ok: false`) and compiled by the engine.

globals.description: Installed as guest globals: own keys that are identifiers, do not start with `__` and are not `__proto__`/`constructor`/`prototype`. A key that would shadow a name the runner's own guest program uses is refused as `invalid_request` — the request is malformed, not the script — and the list here is `SCRIPT_REFUSED_GLOBALS` in `zipp-script.ts`, which a test holds to this one.

prepare.description: A preamble function that maps the parsed globals (`program`/`body`/`auto`) or the args array (`entry`) before the source runs.

pythonJob.description: A Python project, spelled out (`files`, `entry`, `call`) or named (`modes` plus the author's `source`, unfolded by the runner from the request's profile). Never both: two ways to build one project is an ambiguity, and it is refused rather than resolved.

modes.description: Modes of the request's `profile.python.modes`, tried in order on their own fresh Engines; the next is tried only when the engine reported `source` while the project initialised. The failure reported is the last attempt's, with THAT mode's `lineOffset` applied. A name the profile does not define refuses the whole request.

source.description: The author's text, wrapped by whichever mode is running. `modes` only.

entry.description: The module whose top level runs.

call.description: A top-level function of `entry`, called with `args`.

fallbackOnSourceError.description: Tried once, on a fresh Engine, when `files` fails to compile or its top level raises (the engine's `source` kind). Same `entry` and `call`. A job that names `modes` says the same thing as a second mode in the list, and gets the second phase's own line arithmetic with it; this shape carries a whole replacement file set and no arithmetic, and stays exactly as it was for the jobs that use it.
